source: Fiorineschi, Frillici, Rotini (2018) Supporting systematic conceptual design with TRIZ (DESIGN 2018)
finding: Claims the FDM creativity gap: FDM gives non-comprehensive support to innovative solutions (citing Tomiyama 2009), so some scholars added TRIZ. The paper says these integrations hit non-negligible issues and proposes an alternative.
numbers: Conceptual-design phase is said to fix about 80% of product costs (Ullman 2010 cited). Three academic examples, no controlled experiment, no sample.
limits: Design paper with worked examples only; the 'gap' is argued from literature, not measured.
agent_relevance: The scaffold's own claim 'FDM misses creativity' rests on literature argument, not on an experiment. Treat as [S].

source: Fiorineschi et al. (2018) DESIGN paper, section 2.1-2.2 background
finding: TRIZ rests on solving technical contradictions with 40 Inventive Principles, plus a Subject-Action-Object (SAO) function model. FDM rests on Energy-Material-Signal (EMS) flows, function structures and morphological charts (rows = functions, columns = working principles).
numbers: Problems are sorted into 3 SAO classes: subject-missing (SM), performance (PP), harmful effect (HE). EMS model has no subject, so SAO cannot be built from a function structure.
limits: Definitions only. Authors state TRIZ takes long to learn (Malmqvist 1996) and only limited tool sets are used in industry (Moehrle 2005; Ilevbare 2013; Spreafico and Russo 2016).
agent_relevance: Typed problem classes (SM, PP, HE) could route a problem to a typed reframe operator: this is a code-checkable classification.

source: Fiorineschi et al. (2018) DESIGN paper, section 2.3 on integration strategies
finding: Ten TRIZ-FDM integration proposals exist (from the authors' own review). Two strategies: 'support' (apply TRIZ separately: more complex and onerous process) and 'merging' (change FDM or TRIZ: unclear whether original advantages survive). Authors conclude forcing TRIZ into FDM is 'destined to fail or, at least, to face many practical and theoretical issues'.
numbers: 10 proposals, 5 general issues (counts from the 2018 review as cited here). Key blocker: PP and HE problems cannot be identified until a working principle is chosen for a function.
limits: Strong judgement made without data; it is the authors' argument.
agent_relevance: Warns that bolting a creativity tool onto a staged pipeline can add cost without a measured gain. Test before adding.

source: Fiorineschi et al. (2018) DESIGN paper, section 3: PSN as the alternative
finding: Proposes Problem-Solution Network (PSN, Fiorineschi 2016) as the base: problems written as 'How to verb + noun?', co-evolving with solutions; six rules (main task, first-level problems, solution-independent decomposition, abstraction order, branch independence, completeness). SAO triads can be read off PSN branches.
numbers: Six PSN rules; three examples, one per problem class (SM, PP, HE).
limits: No measured outcome. Selection of TRIZ tool is by the authors' expertise, admitted subjective.
agent_relevance: The PSN is a problem-tree with alternating problem and solution nodes. It matches the schema's reframe and branch states; closest published analogue.

source: Fiorineschi et al. (2018) DESIGN paper, examples 4.1 to 4.3
finding: Example SM: clothespin redesign, Ideal Final Result ('clothes fasten by themselves') gave a new solution (clothes held between two twisted wires), used to break design fixation. Example PP: dishwasher, Standard Solution 1.1.2 (add a substance) gave particles in the jet. Example HE: aluminium anodising tub 1 m x 4 m at about 90 C, lid conflicts with bar movement; TRIZ tools sought non-lid solutions.
numbers: One new solution per example; no counts of ideas, no novelty rating, no control group.
limits: Anecdotal. No test of whether FDM alone would have produced the same ideas.
agent_relevance: Gives a concrete form of 'reframe on signal': a stated failing function triggers IFR or standard-solution prompts. Evidence is anecdotal.

source: Fiorineschi et al. (2018) DESIGN paper, section 5 limits
finding: Admits: no guideline yet for putting TRIZ-generated solutions back into the PSN; tool choice is subjective; calls for case studies, interviews and surveys.
numbers: No N reported anywhere in the paper.
limits: Self-declared limits.
agent_relevance: Confirms no controlled TRIZ-with-systematic-design study existed as of 2018 in the authors' own view.

source: Fiorineschi, Frillici, Rotini (2019) Teaching and learning design methods: facing the related issues with TRIZ (ICED19)
finding: Used TRIZ (OTSM contradiction model, separation principles, system operator) to improve a course teaching a systematic conceptual-design method. Six general problems listed; two physical contradictions extracted; eight feasible suggestions produced.
numbers: Course: Mechanical Engineering, Florence, about 20-30 students per year, 3 months; 12 of about 30 conceptual-design hours on the method, only 5 hours lectures. 8 suggestions; 4 (numbers 2,3,4,7) to be implemented next edition.
limits: Authors state the 'most impacting' limit: no information on real feasibility or impact of the suggestions. No outcome data.
agent_relevance: TRIZ used as a meta-tool on the method itself, not on designs. Shows TRIZ contradictions can be applied to process problems; untested.

source: Fiorineschi et al. (2019) ICED19, observed student reaction to systematic method
finding: Six years of teaching experience: students see the method's advantages but find the final project too onerous; many abandon methods later. Cites that industry rarely follows FDM (Maurer and Widmann 2012) and that students drop methods in careers.
numbers: Survey: mandatory anonymous questionnaire plus an extra online survey; no counts given in the paper text.
limits: Self-report, single course, single teacher.
agent_relevance: Cost of method use is a real adoption barrier; a scaffold that costs tokens per step has the same shape of problem.

source: Jiang, Luo et al. (2024) AutoTRIZ DETC2024 (DETC2024-143166), consistency experiment
finding: LLM (GPT-4, version 20231106) runs the TRIZ chain: problem, contradiction, matrix lookup, principles, solutions. Reasoning flow is controlled by code; the matrix lookup is a fixed function module. Contradiction detection tested on 10 textbook cases, 100 runs each.
numbers: 10 cases from 7 textbooks; 100 trials per case; entropy of the contradiction pair distribution (range 0 to 6.64); 7 of 10 cases match or half-match the textbook within the top 3 detections; cases 5, 6, 7, 8 show one dominant answer.
limits: Human textbook answer is not a gold standard (authors say so). Only 10 cases. No quality rating of the ideas. Contradiction choice is unstable in most cases.
agent_relevance: Same design as our program-decides, model-fills-slots rule. But the LLM's contradiction pick is noisy; a code check or vote on that slot is needed (G4: samples are not independent).

source: Jiang et al. (2024) AutoTRIZ, case 7 comparison with textbook
finding: Case 7 (metal shots in plastic pipes): textbook chose improving param Speed (9), worsening Stability of composition (13), principle 28 Mechanical Substitution, solution: magnet at the elbow. AutoTRIZ picked other principles and gave different, practical solutions. Authors call both practical.
numbers: One case compared; no scores.
limits: Qualitative only. No blind expert rating.
agent_relevance: Different principle gives different solution: the matrix adds distinct directions, but that is shown by one example only.

source: Jiang, Li, Qian, Zhang, Luo (2025) AutoTRIZ v4 preprint, battery thermal case
finding: Case study: battery thermal management for e-VTOL / EV. Contradiction found between shape/contact area and energy loss, which matched experts. Proposed design (air cooling with flat heat pipe, FHP-BTMS) reported 20-30% better grouping efficiency and volumetric energy density and more than 60% better thermal management efficiency; Table 1 shows +24%, +64%, +26% versus best existing scheme.
numbers: Single design case, computed metrics from the authors' own model, 2 existing schemes compared.
limits: Author-run, author-computed, one case. ChatGPT guided to use TRIZ directly 'always included apparent errors, such as mismatched contradictions and inventive principles' (anecdote, no counts).
agent_relevance: Supports a code-enforced matrix step over free LLM TRIZ: the unconstrained model mismatched contradictions to principles. Evidence is anecdotal.

source: Jiang et al. (2025) AutoTRIZ v4, limits
finding: Authors list: LLM output may hallucinate; no objective mechanism to rate solution quality; only 40 principles; user still needs domain knowledge to read the report. Evaluation relies on 10 textbook cases and one design case.
numbers: n=10 cases; 100 trials each.
limits: Preprint v4 dated 2025-03-24; no human-subject test and no baseline arm (plain LLM without TRIZ) with scores.
agent_relevance: No published equal-token test of TRIZ-scaffold vs plain LLM here. That test is still open for us.

source: Chen, Song, Ding, Sun, Childs, Zuo (2024) TRIZ-GPT (DETC2024-143163), setup
finding: Workflow: problem restatement, parameter mapping, contradiction analysis (step 3), inventive solution reasoning (step 4). Four prompt strategies tested: basic, chain-of-thought (CoT), few-shot, CoT plus few-shot. Cases split by GPT-4 training cutoff (April 2023) to avoid leakage.
numbers: Collection A: 37 classic cases (3 used for few-shot, 34 tested); collection B: 10 cases after April 2023; 84 case-solution comparisons for step 4; average of 5.5 contradiction pairs per B case.
limits: Ground truth contradiction pairs annotated by one researcher, reviewed by another. Solution quality was NOT rated by experts (judged impractical across fields).
agent_relevance: Shows how to test on post-cutoff cases; we should copy that to avoid leakage.

source: Chen et al. (2024) TRIZ-GPT, contradiction analysis results
finding: CoT prompting gave the best recall of human-labelled contradiction pairs: 0.691 (GPT-4). Recall was above precision, so output is broad and diverse. In 85.3% of cases (basic prompt) and 88.2% (CoT), GPT-4 matched at least half of the parameters in the labelled pairs.
numbers: 34 cases from collection A; four prompt strategies; few-shot recall lower, authors guess the model copied the number of pairs from examples.
limits: Single annotator pipeline; recall is the main metric so over-generation is rewarded.
agent_relevance: LLM finds the right TRIZ parameters often but also adds many extra ones; a program-side filter is needed.

source: Chen et al. (2024) TRIZ-GPT, GPT-4 vs GPT-3.5 on post-cutoff cases
finding: On 10 cases published after GPT-4's training data, CoT recall was 0.544 (GPT-4) against 0.400 (GPT-3.5). Both models produced more pairs than the 5.5 average. GPT-3.5 sometimes left out the TRIZ parameter numbers that were requested.
numbers: Collection B n=10; recall 0.544 vs 0.400. GPT-4 CoT recall on old cases was 0.691 vs 0.544 on new cases (different collections, so not a clean comparison).
limits: Small n, no significance test. Drop from 0.691 to 0.544 might be leakage or case difficulty; the paper does not separate them.
agent_relevance: Possible sign of memorisation on classic TRIZ cases. Our tests must use fresh problems.

source: Chen et al. (2024) TRIZ-GPT, solution similarity metric
finding: Cosine similarity between generated and original solutions was high and flat across prompt strategies: Base M=0.829 (SD 0.031), CoT 0.823 (0.031), few-shot 0.824 (0.030), CoT+few-shot 0.824 (0.033). Authors chose few-shot for structure and token cost.
numbers: 84 cases; all means above 0.82; differences about 0.006.
limits: Cosine similarity to a known solution measures closeness, not creativity or quality; high similarity may mean no novelty. No expert rating.
agent_relevance: Similarity-to-ground-truth is the wrong metric for a creativity gap. Use distinctness count (our planned test).

source: Chen et al. (2024) TRIZ-GPT, in-pipe robot case study
finding: Case study (in-pipe robot, aims: fewer motors, adapt to pipe diameter) applied TRIZ principles 1 Segmentation and 11 Beforehand Cushioning; GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 solutions compared by keyword coding against original solutions.
numbers: One case, keyword coding only.
limits: Author-coded, one case; the paper lists proprietary-data scarcity and bias/overfitting as open limits.
agent_relevance: Anecdotal support only.

source: Ghane, Ang, Cavallucci et al. (2023) Semantic TRIZ systematic review (Heliyon 10(1) e23775)
finding: Systematic review of AI and NLP in TRIZ, Jan 2009 to Mar 2022. Of 57 papers, only 12 clearly discussed benefits or limits and 31 did not address them. About 18% addressed AI-supported ideation; 62% focused on TRIZ tools (function analysis 19%, evolution trends 13%).
numbers: 1,136 records after dedup, 428 by title, 231 by abstract, 106 full text, 57 included. 68% used semantic analysis; 25% syntactic plus semantic; 32% used SAO structures.
limits: Covers pre-LLM work only (to March 2022). Page text was long; I read about the first 100,000 characters.
agent_relevance: Pre-LLM TRIZ automation was mostly patent mining, not idea quality tests.

source: Wang and Uzzi (2026) TRIZBench: Inventive Problem Solving with LLMs (ACL Findings 2026)
finding: Benchmark from open technical sources and US patents with three tasks: contradiction prediction, inventive principle prediction, grounded TRIZ reasoning. Detecting a contradiction is easier than picking the right trade-off pair; principle prediction improves when TRIZ structure is used explicitly. Says earlier TRIZ-LLM evaluations were small, narrow, rarely used patent text.
numbers: Abstract page only: benchmark size, models and scores not stated on the page I opened.
limits: Only the abstract was read, no tables.
agent_relevance: Supports structured (matrix-guided) prediction over free prediction, consistent with AutoTRIZ. Numbers still to fetch.

source: Cok, Motte, Hmina, El Hassani, Demsar, Tavcar, Vukasinovic (2026) Evaluating TRIZ with and without LLM support (PDS 2026, DOI 10.1017/pds.2026.10409)
finding: Experiment with engineering students, 3 problems, TRIZ contradiction matrix with and without an LLM. LLM did not consistently give better designs on complex tasks. It lowered mental effort, improved grasp of contradictions and raised perceived usefulness. Prompting skill strongly affected results.
numbers: Participant count and statistics not on the page I opened (abstract only).
limits: Abstract-level only; direction of effects, no effect sizes.
agent_relevance: One of the few human-subject tests: LLM help eased effort but did not raise design quality on hard tasks. Fetch full paper.

source: Xu, Wu, Zhao (2026) TRIZ-RAGNER (arXiv 2602.23656)
finding: Retrieval-augmented LLM tags improving and worsening parameters in patent sentences (PaTRIZ dataset) with dense retrieval, cross-encoder rerank and structured prompting.
numbers: Precision 85.6%, recall 82.9%, F1 84.2%; +7.3 F1 points over the prompt-enhanced GPT baseline (about 76.9).
limits: Abstract only. Extraction from patents, not idea generation.
agent_relevance: Grounding the LLM in a TRIZ knowledge base beat plain prompting on a typed slot: retrieval for typed slots.

source: Lee, Jeong, Yoo, Yang, Kang (2026) TRIZ-inspired text-to-CAD (arXiv 2606.21378)
finding: LLM generates editable chair CAD models, then TRIZ principles (segmentation, anti-weight, dynamics, composite materials) make variants. Optimisation stage not implemented.
numbers: 4.0-14.7% mass reduction across enhanced designs; no creativity metric, no baseline stated in abstract.
limits: Abstract only; creativity claimed qualitatively.
agent_relevance: Reports an engineering metric, not a creativity one.

source: Szczepanik and Chudziak (2025) TRIZ Agents multi-agent LLM (arXiv 2506.18783)
finding: Multi-agent LLM system where agents take TRIZ roles for innovation tasks. Search listing shows qualitative results only.
numbers: No numbers in the listing I saw.
limits: Listing only; not read.
agent_relevance: No quantitative evidence.

source: Trapp and Warschat (2024) LLM-based extraction of contradictions from patents (arXiv 2403.14258)
finding: GPT-4 with one detailed prompt maps patent contradiction text to the 39 TRIZ engineering parameters, instead of fine-tuned models.
numbers: No performance numbers in the listing.
limits: Listing only; not read.
agent_relevance: Typed mapping task, shows the matrix can be fed by an LLM.

source: Spreafico and Russo (2016) TRIZ industrial case studies: a critical survey (Procedia CIRP 39, 51-56)
finding: Search-result abstract: more than 200 case studies from the TRIZ Journal and ETRIA TRIZ Future Conference were collected and analysed. Cited by the 2018 DESIGN paper for the finding that only a limited set of TRIZ tools is used in industry.
numbers: More than 200 case studies (lower bound from abstract snippet).
limits: Full text blocked by repository; not read. Case sources are self-selected practitioner venues.
agent_relevance: Reported TRIZ successes come from venues that publish successes; selection bias.

source: Fiorineschi, Frillici, Rotini (2018) Enhancing functional decomposition and morphology with TRIZ: literature review (Computers in Industry 94, 1-15)
finding: First literature review on TRIZ with FDM. Per the 2018 DESIGN paper (which I read), it found 10 integration proposals and 5 general issues; the most critical were differing TRIZ-tool interpretations and basic TRIZ/FDM differences.
numbers: 10 proposals, 5 issues (second-hand, from the DESIGN 2018 text). Crossref lists 73 citing works.
limits: Full text blocked by Cloudflare; not opened.
agent_relevance: Backbone for the founding claim; the review itself should be read before citing.

source: Fiorineschi, Frillici, Rotini (2018) Exploiting TRIZ tools for enhancing systematic conceptual design activities (J Eng Des 29(6), 259-290)
finding: Combines TRIZ tools with the PSN conceptual-design approach. Not read; only metadata and search snippet seen.
numbers: Crossref lists 44 citing works.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Likely the full version of the DESIGN 2018 proposal; read next.

source: Ilevbare, Probert, Phaal (2013) A review of TRIZ and its benefits and challenges in practice (Technovation 33, 30-37)
finding: Cited by the 2018 DESIGN paper and by TRIZ-GPT as showing that detailed success and failure cases of TRIZ use are seldom shared, and that only a limited tool set is used.
numbers: Crossref lists 428 citing works.
limits: Not opened; second-hand claims only.
agent_relevance: The standard critical review of TRIZ practice; read next.

source: Jiang et al. (2025) AutoTRIZ v4, background claim on TRIZ origin
finding: States TRIZ was developed in the 1960s by Altshuller and colleagues from analysis of over 40,000 patents, finding repeated patterns of innovation; toolkit includes trimming, evolution trends and 76 standard solutions; 40 principles, 39 engineering parameters.
numbers: Over 40,000 patents; 40 principles; 39 parameters; 76 standard solutions.
limits: Secondary statement (Altshuller 1984/1999 itself not opened). Patent counts vary across sources.
agent_relevance: Foundation facts for the matrix: the contradiction matrix is a 39 by 39 lookup.
